sender.en: “Pakistan Post” or a courier company, from an unknown number

name.en: Fake Pakistan Post or courier SMS: “update your address” or “share the code”

how.en: An SMS claims to be from Pakistan Post or another courier, often with a tracking number. It says your parcel could not be delivered because of an address problem and asks you to update your details urgently through a link. The link opens a copy of a courier site that steals your personal and card details, or asks you to download a file. Other courier messages ask you to enter or share a verification code, which can give scammers access to your accounts.

text.en: An SMS from “Pakistan Post” or a courier says your parcel is held.
You must update your address urgently or the parcel returns.
A link leads to a fake courier page or a file to install.
The page asks for card details, or you are asked for a code.
Pakistan Post: Your package is held at our warehouse due to incomplete address information. Please update your address within 24 hours or it will be returned: [link]
TCS: Your parcel is ready for delivery. Share the verification code sent to your number with our rider to receive it.

en: pakistan post sms update address link
package will be returned update details sms
courier sms asked card payment for redelivery
A delivery message you weren’t expecting, with a link.
A request for card details or a small fee to redeliver.
Couriers asking you to share or enter a code.
Don’t click; check tracking on the courier’s official website or app.
Never share codes sent to your phone.
If you entered card details, call your bank; report the number to PTA.
